claim_text: The European Commission confirms it was hit by a cyberattack first detected on Oct 22
summary: A Commission spokesperson told journalists on Nov 19 that the first signs of the attack were detected on Oct 22, and called it an 'AI-generated cyber campaign'.
detail: The Record and The Brussels Times each report the briefing; The Register says the Commission first publicly acknowledged the cyberattack that day.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three outlets report the spokesperson confirming the attack and the Oct 22 date.

claim_text: The Commission says the attackers used AI tools
summary: The spokesperson said: 'Indeed we can confirm that this was done with AI tools.' The spokesperson did not name the tool.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Both outlets report the spokesperson saying AI tools were used.

claim_text: CERT-EU reportedly identified ARTEX, a public AI hacking framework, as a tool used
summary: The Record and The Brussels Times both say Politico, citing an EU official, reported that CERT-EU identified the use of ARTEX, a publicly available AI-powered tool for finding and exploiting weaknesses.
detail: The Commission has not named the tool on the record in anything we read.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Both outlets attribute this to one report by Politico.
notes: Outlets repeating one report count as one source.

claim_text: Nobody has been officially named as the attacker
summary: The spokesperson declined to identify those responsible, saying the investigation was still ongoing.
detail: We did not find an official attribution, and no group has claimed the attack in anything we read. We did not open leak or dark-web sites.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The Brussels Times reports the refusal to name anyone; The Register says the Commission would not make conclusive statements while the investigation goes on.

claim_text: The Commission says an incident on its EU Academy platform involves users' personal data
summary: The EU Academy site says: 'The European Commission has detected a cybersecurity incident on its EU Academy platform involving personal data of EU Academy users.' It warns of a possible loss of user data.
detail: EU Academy is the Commission's online learning platform with courses on EU policies. The notice asks users to watch for suspicious emails, spearphishing and impersonation.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Commission's own notice on the EU Academy site states it.

claim_text: Names and email addresses of EU Academy users outside the EU institutions were stolen
summary: The Commission's spokesperson said at a Nov 23 briefing that EU Academy was among the systems compromised and that names and email addresses of its users, people outside the EU institutions, were among the data taken.
detail: The Register, AP and SecurityWeek each report this from the briefing. The spokesperson did not say how many people were affected and said the exact scale of the leak is still under investigation.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Three outlets with their own reporting (The Register, AP, SecurityWeek) each report the spokesperson saying names and email addresses were taken.
notes: Was Reported on The Register alone; relabelled Confirmed on Nov 25 when AP and SecurityWeek were added.

claim_text: The Commission says it found no evidence of a data breach affecting its staff broadly
summary: The Record and The Brussels Times say the spokesperson said investigators found no evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole. The Record says the spokesperson was unaware of any ransom demand.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Both outlets report the Commission's own statement, so it rests on the Commission's word.

claim_text: Most affected Commission systems are back, but EU Academy is offline
summary: The Brussels Times says most affected services had been restored by Nov 19; The Register says some remained unavailable that day. The EU Academy notice says public access to the platform has been disabled.
detail: Reports say the disruption mainly hit internal tools, including the HR system that handles pay and leave, and the medical reimbursement system.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The Commission's notice says EU Academy access is disabled; two outlets report most other services restored.
notes: Re-check the EU Academy site on every run.

claim_text: EU Academy's site also says the platform is offline for a rebuild until Jan 14
summary: A separate notice on the EU Academy site says the platform will be offline from 11 November 2026 to 14 January 2027 while a new platform is built, and that all users must create a new account.
detail: The Register says it asked whether the downtime and the new accounts are connected to the cyberattack, and a spokesperson did not answer those points.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The notice is on the Commission's own site; The Register reports it.
notes: Whether the rebuild is linked to the attack is not known.

claim_text: The Commission says it informed affected people and the EU data protection supervisor
summary: The Record says the Commission had notified affected individuals and was in touch with CERT-EU and the European Data Protection Supervisor. The Register quotes the supervisor confirming it was 'informed and notified in phases'.
detail: For EU Academy, The Register says the Commission posted a general notice on the website rather than contacting users one by one.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Two outlets report the statements; each rests on what the Commission and the supervisor said.

claim_text: Euronews reports the Commission suspects a China-backed group; the Commission has not attributed the attack
summary: Euronews, citing two sources with knowledge of the matter, says the Commission suspects a China-backed group, codenamed 'Panda' internally. The Commission says there is no attribution until its investigation ends.
detail: Euronews says the suspicion rests on the attack's sophistication and on the use of ARTEX, which it calls a Chinese-developed AI tool for finding weaknesses. It quotes the spokesperson: 'for now, no attribution from our side.' No other outlet we read has its own sources for the suspicion.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Euronews reports the suspicion from two unnamed sources and quotes the Commission declining to attribute.
notes: One outlet, unnamed sources; not an official attribution.

claim_text: Euronews reports the attack was not fully contained on Nov 23 and EU Academy was taken offline on Nov 21
summary: Euronews (Nov 23) says that a month after the attack began the Commission had yet to fully contain the breach, and took the EU Academy website offline on Saturday, Nov 21. Some internal apps remain unavailable.
detail: The Register reports the spokesperson declined to make conclusive statements while the investigation continues. Whether the earlier rebuild notice (offline from Nov 11) and the Nov 21 shutdown are the same event is not known.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Euronews states the breach was not fully contained and gives the day the site was taken offline.
notes: One outlet; the Commission has not said whether the attack is over.
